note: PASS WITH CAVEATS, built as the direct sibling peters_2025_gen_risk_strength (batch_133) and following batch_385's conventions. (1) SOURCE/MAPPING: the DMQs sheet 'id' column holds the raw LimeSurvey/CSV column names GenEvHospital and GenEvSymptoms; data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py matches ^Gen(Ex|Ev)(.+)$, routes Ev to gen_risk_eval and lower-cases the tail (name-preserving rename, core model s3 pattern 2), so 2/2 live codes (hospital, symptoms) reconstruct from the sheet's own ids with no order inference; the codes are also self-describing. Step 3b: raa_construct reads 'Generic Belief' for all GenEv rows and the Ev (evaluation) component matches the table name and dictionary description ('belief evaluation component'). (2) STRUCTURE: item_text is the sheet's subquestion_en ('I prefer to ...' for hospital, 'I prefer to get ...' for symptoms); the item's referent is completed by its anchor pair in option_text. instructions and section_prompt blank: the sheet publishes no separate participant instruction for this block. (3) OPTIONS: scale_type uni for both; DMQ_scales states codes 1..5 displayed (1)..(5), 0 = '(not applicable)' dropped by the IRW script. Only endpoints carry verbal labels, so resp 2-4 ship with option_text blank, not padded. Anchors taken from bottom_anchor_bare/top_anchor_bare (bottom_anchor_en/top_anchor_en append '(1)'/'(5)'; stripping that is the only deviation). (4) ITEM COUNT: the sheet defines three GenEv items; GenEvDie ('I prefer to ...' certainly not die/certainly die) is absent from the live table. In the three raw export files fetched (sid 100103 rids 1-1479, sid 100105 rids 1-2450, sid 100110 rids 13027-13135; 4,038 rows) GenEvDie has 0 non-empty cells while GenExDie has 81 and GenEvHospital 11, so the item appears never to have been collected in its original wording; not checked across all 50 files. No rows are shipped for die. (5) AMENDED VARIANTS NOT IN THIS TABLE: the DMQ_amendments sheet (key 1gT10SXZ9YsFrRjRuIMsE8aDH916fClizqcBFuz_q6D0, cached by the batch_133 gnrc_beliefs agent) defines GenEvHospital2 / GenEvSymptoms2 / GenEvDie2 with different stems ('For me, avoiding that I end up in the hospital is ...', 'For me, avoiding coronavirus symptoms is ...', anchors 'not particularly desirable'..'extremely desirable'). These are separate raw columns absent from the processing script's ITEM_POLARITY, so this table holds original-wording responses only; verify check B confirms live counts match GenEvHospital, not GenEvHospital2 (sid 100103: live 6/0/1/0/0 = raw GenEvHospital 6/0/1/0/0 vs GenEvHospital2 5/1/2/2/8). Respondents who received the amended wording are therefore not in this table. (6) DESIGN: 2,130 rows from 2,110 ids; only 20 ids answered both items, so each respondent mostly saw one of the two (consistent with the tool's per-respondent belief sampling); not a duplication. (7) LANGUAGE: per the 2026-09-11 multi-language ruling, `language` (placed after `instrument`) lists every language in this table's cov_language, named plainly and ordered by response-row count in the live data (local irw cache, no new export), ties broken alphabetically: English; Dutch; Italian; Turkish; Romanian; French; Greek; Indonesian; Spanish; Amharic; Chinese (Simplified); Arabic; Portuguese (Brazil); German; Portuguese -- 15 languages (en 1038 rows, nl 935, it 66, tr 21, ro 18, fr 13, el 9, id 9, es 9, am 3, zh-Hans 3, ar 2, pt-BR 2, de 1, pt 1; 0 rows with missing cov_language). Base text fields hold the English source-language version only (the project's master text and the version read by the largest group, 1038 of 2130 rows); respondents in the other 14 languages read translations held in the other worksheets of the same DMQs sheet, which are not shipped, so the _translated columns are omitted and text_source=study_materials. (8) RIGHTS: governed by the existing instrument_rights_register.csv row for the YCR DMQs (verdict allow, 2026-09-10), resting on the paper's statement 'everything produced in this project is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution licenses or similarly'; applied, not re-derived.
public_note: Both items share the evaluation stem 'I prefer to (get) ...' and are completed by their endpoint anchors (resp=1 'certainly not end up in a hospital' / 'no symptoms', resp=5 'certainly end up in a hospital' / 'severe symptoms'); intermediate points were not verbally labelled. The source defines a third item (dying) that has no responses in this table, and countries that received the amended wording ('For me, avoiding ... is ...') are not included. Respondents answered in 15 languages (listed in the language column); only the English source wording is shipped, so most non-English respondents read a translation of it, and each respondent's language is in cov_language.

note: PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_386, 2026-09-24). 14 rows = 7 items x resp {0,1}; validate_items.R --table-sets passes item and resp sets. (1) STEP 3b: this is NOT a DMQ/RAA table. It is built by data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_precautions.py from the LimeSurvey multiple-choice (checkbox, type M) question hwFrequency, one of the tool's 'REQ' questions defined in a separate REQs sheet (not the DMQs sheet used by the batch_133/134/385 siblings). Content matches the table name and the dictionary Description ('hand-washing situations/frequency checklist (7 items, binary)'): the question asks in which situations the respondent regularly washes hands. (2) MAPPING: the script matches raw columns ^hwFrequency\.([a-zA-Z]+)\.$ and lower-cases the group (snzCf -> snzcf) -- a name-preserving rename, no positional step. The REQs sheet keys each option text by ls_answer_code, which is the LimeSurvey subquestion title and the raw column infix; 7/7 codes reconstruct, and 7/7 texts are identical in the sheet and in the deployed English v1.10 survey file. Recorded paper_explicit rather than data_labels by the sibling convention (companion instrument-definition sheet, not the export header). Step 5b VERIFIED: cell-level re-run over sid 100110's raw exports reproduces 65198/65198 cells, 0 disagreements (verify_peters_2025_hw_frequency.R). (3) STRUCTURE: the question stem 'Do you regularly wash or clean your hands in the following situations?' applies to every item and is recorded once in instructions; section_prompt blank (group handWashingGroup1 has no description; question help empty). item_text = the checkbox option label. Single trivial section_id; correct_response blank. (4) OPTIONS: resp 1 = option ticked (raw 'Y'), resp 0 = not ticked, per the processing script. A checkbox has no printed response labels, so option_text is BLANK for both resp values rather than IRW-authored 'selected'/'not selected' text; the 0/1 meaning is stated in public_note. (5) SOURCE QUIRKS KEPT VERBATIM: 'somone' (typo for 'someone') in cntct, as in both the sheet and the deployed English survey; surfc's parenthetical 'e.g., doorknobs, railings, tables, buttons/switches' as printed. 'never' is not an exclusive option in the survey definition (no exclude_all_others attribute): in the live table 816 of the 2849 respondents who ticked 'never' also ticked at least one situation. (6) LANGUAGE: per the 2026-09-11 multi-language ruling, language lists all 22 cov_language values in the live table by response share (rows = 7 x respondents; respondent counts en 32829, nl 25260, ro 5857, it 1974, tr 1478, pt-BR 1463, fr 802, es 364, id 280, el 241, pt 212, de 118, zh-Hans 74, ar 49, hu 47, am 35, pl 25, zh-Hant-HK 20, ja 19, ur 12, ko 4, he 3; none missing). Base fields hold the English master text (read by the en respondents, 46.1% of 71166); the other deployments read translations held in the same production survey files (e.g. Dutch 'Was je regelmatig je handen in de volgende situaties?'), not shipped, so no _translated columns and text_source=study_materials. (7) RIGHTS: applied the existing instrument_rights_register.csv row 'Your COVID-19 Risk (YCR) Decisional Mechanism Questions (DMQs) -- governs all nine peters_2025_* IRW tables' (verdict allow, 2026-09-10), whose notes extend it to 'any remaining sibling' and which rests on the paper's grant that 'everything produced in this project is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution licenses'; the REQs sheet is produced by the same project. Not re-derived. (8) DATA OBSERVATION (not a defect): every one of the 71166 respondents has all 7 items (498162 rows = 7 x 71166) because the script gates on the *Est equation column, which LimeSurvey fills for everyone who reached the page whether or not they ticked anything; the question was not mandatory, so resp 0 cannot distinguish 'not ticked' from 'skipped the question'. 1389 respondents ticked nothing at all (all 7 = 0). In sid 100110, 9314 of 13135 raw rows pass the Est gate. RETRY TEST: N/A, clean pass.
public_note: These seven items are the tick-boxes of one select-all-that-apply question ('Do you regularly wash or clean your hands in the following situations?'): resp 1 means the box was ticked and resp 0 that it was not, which also covers respondents who skipped the question, and the boxes carried no response labels, so option_text is blank. The tool was fielded in 22 languages and only the English master wording is shipped (per-respondent language is in cov_language); the English original misspells 'someone' as 'somone' in item cntct, kept as printed.

note: PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_386, 2026-09-24). 8 rows, 4 items x resp {0,1}; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets. (1) STEP 3b / SOURCE: this is NOT a DMQ/RAA table. It is built by data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_precautions.py (the follow-up to _dcts.py) from the LimeSurvey checkboxes question hwIntensity: one raw column hwIntensity.<code>. per option, 'Y' -> resp=1, blank -> resp=0, gated on the paired hwIntensity<Code>Est column being non-null. So the source is the project's REQs sheet (the non-DMQ 'required questions'), not the DMQs sheet. The table name and dictionary Description ('hand-washing intensity/thoroughness checklist (4 items, binary)') match the content; no mismatch. (2) MAPPING: code derivation is pattern 1/2 -- the IRW code is the raw export column's option code, lower-cased (the codes durtn/soap/thrgh/none are already lower case, so the rename is the identity); no positional step. The REQs sheet ties each ls_answer_code to its text_en explicitly: 4/4 live codes match 4/4 sheet answer options, 0 either way. Recorded as paper_explicit rather than data_labels for the same reason as the DMQ siblings: the sheet is a companion instrument-definition file, not the response export's own header. Step 5b VERIFIED (verify_peters_2025_hw_intensity.R, VERDICT: PASS). (3) STRUCTURE: a single check-all question. instructions = the question's own text_en 'If you wash/clean your hands, how do you do this?'; each checkbox option is an item and its option text is item_text, verbatim (incl. 'handsanitiser' as one word and the curly apostrophe in 'I don’t do any of the above'). LimeSurvey's generic checkbox tip is UI chrome, not in the sheet, and is not shipped (the build script sets hide_tip='0' while the deployed .lss carries hide_tip=Y, so whether respondents saw it is unclear). Single trivial section_id; section_prompt and correct_response NA. (4) OPTIONS: resp 1 = option checked, 0 = not checked. The source prints no labels for checkbox states, so option_text is left NA for both levels (not padded, not invented as 'Selected'); the coding is stated in public_note. (5) LANGUAGE: per the 2026-09-11 multi-language ruling, language lists the 22 cov_language codes present in this table, ordered by response share (distinct respondent ids: en 32200, nl 25018, ro 5759, it 1954, pt-BR 1450, tr 1429, fr 779, es 358, id 277, el 238, pt 207, de 118, zh-Hans 68, ar 49, hu 46, am 35, pl 24, zh-Hant-HK 20, ja 19, ur 12, ko 4, he 2; 70,066 ids, every id has all 4 items, 280,264 rows; row order identical). Base fields hold the English master wording, which the English deployment read and every other version was translated from; text_source=study_materials, no _translated columns. Translation note: the Dutch deployment's thrgh reads 'Ik maak tussen mijn nagels en tussen mijn vingers schoon' ('between my nails', not 'under'), so the Dutch respondents (36% of ids) read a slightly different item. (6) DATA DEFECTS / QUIRKS (response table, for the orchestrator): (a) 'none' is not enforced as exclusive -- the .lss carries no exclude_all_others attribute -- and 48 of 866 respondents who checked 'none' also checked a substantive option (14 one, 8 two, 26 all three); (b) 540 respondents (0.77%) have all four items at 0, i.e. checked nothing; because the Est gate is non-null whenever the page was reached (the .lss Est expression returns a constant when the box is empty), a respondent who skipped the non-mandatory question is coded 0 on every option, indistinguishable from 'not selected'; (c) the build script's hwIntnsDiligence equation tests hwFreqSum==3 rather than hwIntnsSum -- a source scoring bug that does not affect the item responses. (7) RIGHTS: governed by the existing instrument_rights_register.csv YCR row (verdict allow, 2026-09-10). Its title names the DMQs, but its clause is the paper's grant that 'everything produced in this project is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution licenses or similarly' and its notes extend it to 'any remaining sibling'; the REQs sheet is produced by the same project and named in the same CC0 build script. Applied, not re-derived. RETRY TEST: N/A, clean pass.
public_note: This is a single check-all-that-apply question ('If you wash/clean your hands, how do you do this?'): each item is one checkbox option, resp=1 means the option was checked and resp=0 that it was not, so a respondent who skipped the question is coded 0 on all four (540 of 70,066 respondents) and 'I don’t do any of the above' was not enforced as exclusive (48 respondents checked it alongside another option). Respondents answered in 22 languages (listed in the language column); only the English master wording is shipped, and each respondent's language is in cov_language.
